es.summary: El AUD es una enfermedad crónica caracterizada por consumo compulsivo de alcohol, pérdida de control y síntomas de abstinencia.
key_points: Se diagnostica mediante criterios clínicos y herramientas como AUDIT.
BAC ≥0.08% indica consumo de riesgo y posible intoxicación.
El manejo incluye terapia conductual y fármacos como naltrexona.
Complicaciones graves incluyen hepatitis alcohólica y síndrome de abstinencia.
La hidratación y el equilibrio electrolítico son prioridades de enfermería.

pathophysiology: El etanol actúa sobre GABA y NMDA, aumentando la inhibición neuronal.
Repetida exposición genera tolerancia y dependencia neuroquímica.
Se produce adaptación dopaminérgica que refuerza el consumo.
La abstinencia desencadena hiperexcitabilidad del SNC.
risk_factors: Inicio temprano del consumo y estrés crónico.
signs_symptoms: Ansia intensa y pérdida de control al beber.
Irritabilidad, temblor y sudoración al intentar abstenerse.
Náuseas, vómitos y alteración del sueño.
BAC ≥0.08% (≈5 bebidas hombres, 4 mujeres en pocas horas).
diagnostics: Medición de BAC en sangre o aliento.
Evaluación de electrolitos y función renal.
treatment: Terapia cognitivo‑conductual y grupos de apoyo.
Manejo de abstinencia con benzodiacepinas y tiamina.
Suplementación nutricional y reposición de líquidos.
nursing_care: Evaluar consumo, BAC y signos de abstinencia cada 4 h.
Monitorear ingesta y salida de líquidos; peso diario.
Observar signos de deshidratación y desequilibrio electrolítico.
Administrar medicación prescrita y suplementos de tiamina.
Garantizar entorno seguro para prevenir caídas.
patient_teaching: Establecer metas de reducción gradual del consumo.
Identificar desencadenantes y estrategias de afrontamiento.
Importancia de hidratación (≥2 L/día) y nutrición adecuada.
No conducir bajo efectos del alcohol; buscar apoyo comunitario.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Hidratación: paciente mantendrá ingesta de líquidos ≥2 L/día
Balance hídrico: peso estable ±0.5 kg en 48 h

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno
Ofrecer agua, jugos sin azúcar y soluciones electrolíticas
interventions.rationale: Facilita la reposición de volumen y electrolitos

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de deshidratación (turgor, mucosas, frecuencia cardíaca)
Pesar al paciente diariamente a la misma hora
interventions.rationale: Monitorea cambios en el balance hídrico

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la hidratación durante la abstinencia
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y prevención de complicaciones

interventions.action: Administrar tiamina según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Previene síndrome de Wernicke en consumidores crónicos

outcomes: Electrolitos: Na⁺ y K⁺ dentro de rangos normales (Na 135‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L)
Síntomas: paciente sin manifestaciones de hiponatremia ni hipopotasemia

interventions.action: Solicitar panel de electrolitos cada 24 h mientras esté en abstinencia
Observar signos neuromusculares (espasmos, debilidad, arritmias)
Ofrecer alimentos ricos en potasio (plátano, papas) y sodio según tolerancia
interventions.rationale: Contribuye a la reposición natural de electrolitos

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de electrolitos según orden médica
Educar al paciente sobre hidratación adecuada y dieta balanceada
Documentar resultados de laboratorio y respuesta a intervenciones
interventions.rationale: Facilita seguimiento y ajuste del plan de cuidados

en.summary: AUD is a chronic disease characterized by compulsive alcohol consumption, loss of control, and withdrawal symptoms.
key_points: Diagnosis is made using clinical criteria and tools such as AUDIT.
BAC ≥0.08% indicates risky consumption and possible intoxication.
Management includes behavioral therapy and medications such as naltrexone.
Severe complications include alcoholic hepatitis and withdrawal syndrome.
Hydration and electrolyte balance are nursing priorities.

pathophysiology: Ethyl alcohol acts on GABA and NMDA, increasing neuronal inhibition.
Repeated exposure leads to tolerance and neurochemical dependence.
risk_factors: Early onset of drinking and chronic stress.
signs_symptoms: Intense anxiety and loss of control when drinking.
Irritability, tremor, and sweating when attempting abstinence.
BAC ≥0.08% (≈5 drinks for men, 4 for women in a few hours).
diagnostics: BAC measurement in blood or breath.
Liver function tests (AST, ALT, GGT, CDT).
treatment: Withdrawal management with benzodiazepines and thiamine.
nursing_care: Assess consumption, BAC, and withdrawal signs every 4 h.
Monitor fluid intake and output; daily weight.
Observe for dehydration and electrolyte imbalance.
Administer prescribed medication and thiamine supplements.
Ensure a safe environment to prevent falls.
patient_teaching: Set gradual reduction goals for consumption.
Importance of hydration (≥2 L/day) and adequate nutrition.
Do not drive under the influence; seek community support.

outcomes: Hydration: patient will maintain fluid intake ≥2 L/day
Fluid balance: weight stable ±0.5 kg in 48 h

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of fluid deficit

interventions.action: Offer water, unsweetened juices, and electrolyte solutions
Assess dehydration signs (turgor, mucous membranes, heart rate)
Weigh patient daily at the same time
Educate patient on the importance of hydration during withdrawal
Administer thiamine as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Prevents Wernicke’s syndrome in chronic consumers

outcomes: Electrolytes: Na⁺ and K⁺ within normal ranges (Na 135‑145 mEq/L, K 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L)
Symptoms: patient without signs of hyponatremia or hypokalemia

interventions.action: Order electrolyte panel every 24 h while in withdrawal
Observe neuromuscular signs (spasms, weakness, arrhythmias)
Offer potassium‑rich foods (banana, potatoes) and sodium as tolerated
Administer electrolyte supplements as ordered
Educate patient on adequate hydration and balanced diet
Document laboratory results and response to interventions

key_points.4.quote: Death is attributed to cardiovascular complications, hyperthermia, aspiration, and severe fluid and electrolyte disorders.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Over time, the person can build a tolerance to the alcohol, or the physiological capacity to withstand the effects of a substance with repeated use or exposure.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: AUD is a disease that causes: Craving - a strong need to drink Loss of control - not being able to stop drinking once you've started Negative emotional state - feeling anxious and irritable when you are not drinking

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Substance Withdrawal Symptoms Alcohol Restlessness, sweating, tachycardia, vomiting, irritability, seizures, headache, disorientation

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: They include trouble sleeping, shakiness, irritability, anxiety , depression , restlessness, nausea , and sweating .

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Serum electrolytes Potassium, magnesium, and phosphate abnormalities, particularly with severe dehydration Creatinine Kidney function

sections.complications.0.quote: It may lead to liver diseases , such as alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) and cirrhosis .

sections.complications.2.quote: Mortality rates from withdrawal delirium have been historically as high as 20 percent, but with appropriate medical management, the mortality rate is between 1 and 4 percent.

sections.complications.3.quote: Adverse Effects Hepatitis/hepatotoxicity Drowsiness Headache Peripheral neuropathy Allergic dermatitis Metallic taste Heart failure

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: As there can be electrolyte disturbances from various factors during withdrawal, such as dehydration, the nurse needs to monitor the patient carefully for signs of electrolyte abnormalities.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: By identifying the patient’s need for more effective coping skills in the nursing diagnosis, the nurse starts putting together an action plan with interventions that will support the patient in developing healthy coping skills, reducing their reliance on substances, and preventing relapse.
